The operator-published aggregate count of automated-enforcement outcomes (warnings/violations) for a camera or programme subject over a declared period — a claim carries its `period` and `measure` fields beside the integer value, keyed camera × month or site × quarter as published. Aggregate rows only: never a per-violation, plate, person, trip or citation record (P36.6 / R11-ACQ-10, I8 NEW-7) — the aggregate admission is distinct from the connector-forbidden `camera_count` device-count genre, and Part VIII prohibits the row-level surfaces this predicate deliberately replaces.

The organisation that published this camera-registry artifact — registry PUBLISHER provenance, not an operational role. P32.3 / ADR-122 (SIG-TRUST-003): a publisher label never evidences camera operation, ownership, vendor or access status, and never mints an organisation entity-ref (the OSM contributor label is the canonical case).

The publisher of the source dataset this subject's claims derive from — PUBLISHER provenance, never an operational role. P35.26 / SIG-TRUST-003: the publisher label is recorded as `published_by` (the generic sibling of `camera_registry_publisher` for non-registry sources — e.g. "OpenStreetMap contributors", "EFF & MuckRock — Data Driven (2018)"); it never evidences camera operation, ownership, vendor or access status, and — a provenance role — never mints an organisation entity-ref (ADR-112/ADR-122).

Qualifier: the comparability scope a count claim is asserted at (e.g. metro, city_limits, jurisdiction, statewide). P32.3 / SIG-TRUST-004: counts in different scopes answer different questions — they are retained separately and never adjudicated against each other (a scope mismatch is not a contradiction).

Qualifier: the refinement inside a count_scope (e.g. privately_owned, partner_agency, agency_operated). Two counts differ on detail at the same scope label are still different questions (P32.3 / SIG-TRUST-004).

Qualifier: where the evidence behind a claim came from (e.g. seed_fixture, live_capture). P32.3 / SIG-TRUST-004: seed-fixture material is labelled so no read surface presents it as primary live evidence.

§12.3 integration edge: A pushes a watchlist to B for local matching; matches do NOT return to A (one-way list, no feedback — MUST NOT be modelled as federates_search_to, SIG-ONTO-046). Carrier of 'automated alerts' in the twelve-power-properties map (SIG-ONTO-051).
§12.3 integration edge: A can issue per-incident, consent-gated requests to B's users/devices.
§12.3 integration edge: A grants B legal permission to operate a capability; authority moves, no data does.
§12.3 lifecycle edge: B's deployment supersedes A's for the same capability at the same organization (temporal substitution).
§12.3 lifecycle edge: the product/deployment that replaces another for the same capability at the same organization — the forward pair of replaced_by.

A surveillance-technology category retired from the Atlas of Surveillance upstream taxonomy (SIG-ONTO-059): a vocabulary event keyed on the Atlas version at which the category retired, never a world change — a disappearance is "category retired", not a deployment ending.

A deployment's evidenced end in the world (the device set was decommissioned, the programme cancelled) — reserved lifecycle vocabulary named by the Atlas connector but NEVER emitted: an upstream category disappearance is a vocabulary event (atlas_category_retired), not a world event. Registered so the id is governed vocabulary, not an unowned literal.

A mapping-event row recorded when a previously-seen OSM element vanishes from a later snapshot (event_class 'mapping_event'): the element left the map, which is NOT evidence the physical asset left the street.

The world event of a physical surveillance asset being removed from the street — reserved lifecycle vocabulary named by the OSM connector but never inferred from a map deletion: osm_element_deleted (a mapping event) is the only claim a snapshot diff may emit; removal in the world needs its own evidence. Registered so the id is governed vocabulary, not an unowned literal.

The geometry shape kind a record declares for its subject — a `GeometryKind` member (area | line | point) of the ontology enum (§19, SIG-GEO-003). An automated-traffic-enforcement zone or a published camera programme area is an `area`, never a device point; an enforced route or corridor segment is a `line`. Registered by P36.3 (ACQ-03) so the closed vocabulary accepts the `geometry_kind="area"` values P36.4's programme-area emit and P36.6's ATE zone layers assert.

A published programme-area aggregate subject assertion (the register's own row for one grouping column of a camera-related programme aggregate table — DC's PSA). The subject is the published area bucket the operator groups its programme counts by, never a camera device, a geometry, a registrant, a name, or an address (P36.7 / R11-ACQ-11).

The operator-published aggregate count of programme outcomes — applications received, under review, approved, declined, rebates funded, cameras funded — for a programme-area subject over a declared period. A claim carries its `period` and `measure` fields beside the integer value, plus `series` naming the published measure column when one row fans out into per-status series. Aggregate rows only: never a per-registrant, name, address, location, plate, or device record (P36.7 / R11-ACQ-11) — distinct from `enforcement_count` (enforcement outcomes) and from the connector-forbidden `camera_count` device-count genre.

A recorded geometry-defect marking on a registry-observed subject: the defect class an ingest detector or the append-only correction pass found in the published coordinate pair — `axis_swap` (the pair sits outside the declared extent and the transposed pair sits inside it), `null_island` (the pair is at/near (0,0)), `sign_flip` (the pair sits outside the declared extent and negating exactly one axis lands it inside), or `wrong_jurisdiction` (the pair contradicts the declared extent and no transposition or sign flip rescues it). The observed pair, the declared extent it failed and the detector version ride the claim's evidence; the claim only MARKS the defect — the original coordinate claims stand and any corrected coordinate is a new `camera_latitude`/`camera_longitude` claim citing the originals in `derived_from_claim_ids` (P35.16 / R11-DATA-01, F-322, SIG-GEO-008, SIG-IDENT-004, SIG-ONTO-011).
